pick.headline: Peru votes in the Fujimori-Vargas Llosa runoff
pick.summary: On June 10, 1990, Peruvians voted in the presidential runoff between the novelist Mario Vargas Llosa of the Democratic Front and Alberto Fujimori, an agronomist and political newcomer of the Change 90 movement. Fujimori won decisively.
pick.significance: Fujimori's victory brought in a decade of economic shock therapy, war against the Shining Path, and in 1992 his own 'self-coup' closing Congress. He later fled to Japan and was convicted of human rights abuses and corruption.
pick.fbis: The Latin America report of June 11, 1990, carried election-day reporting from Lima: President Garcia voting as polls opened under tight security, observers calling Vargas Llosa and Fujimori 'almost neck and neck,' and indelible ink dropped in emergency zones because of guerrilla threats to voters.
